why: Starting at i you are forced to collect gameVal[i] + gameVal[i+k] + ...; that is a suffix sum along stride k, so dp[i] = gameVal[i] + dp[i+k] computed right to left, and the answer is the largest dp[i].
hints: Once you pick a start, the rest of the path is forced. Can you reuse the score from a later start?
The score from i equals gameVal[i] plus the score from i + k (or just gameVal[i] if i + k is past the end).
Fill dp from the right in one pass and take the max over all i. O(n) time; you can even do it in place.
pitfalls: You cannot stop early: every landed space counts, including negative ones, so a start near the end may win.
The answer can be negative if every space is negative; initialise the max to -infinity, not 0.
n is up to 10^6: avoid recursion and O(n*k) loops.
statement:
A board is a line of spaces gameVal[0..n-1], each worth some (possibly negative) points. Pick a starting space i. Your piece lands on i, then jumps exactly k spaces right each time, landing on i + k, i + 2k, ... and collecting every landed value, until the next jump would go past the last space. Return the maximum total over all starting spaces.

Worked example: gameVal = [2,-3,4,6,1], k = 2

  • Start 0: lands on 0, 2, 4: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7
  • Start 1: lands on 1, 3: -3 + 6 = 3
  • Start 2: 4 + 1 = 5; start 3: 6; start 4: 1

Answer: 7 (starting at index 0).
